groups.title: Signs of the zodiac
groups.explanation: Each is one of the twelve signs of the western zodiac.

groups.title: Animals of the Chinese zodiac
groups.explanation: The Chinese zodiac runs on a cycle of twelve animals, and these come first.

groups.title: Birthstones
groups.explanation: Each stone is traditionally given to those born in one month of the year.

sources.excerpt: These signs roughly correspond to the astronomical constellations with the following modern names: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces.
The Old Mongol calendar uses the Rat, the Ox, the Leopard, the Hare, the Crocodile, the Serpent, the Horse, the Sheep, the Monkey, the Hen, the Dog and the Hog.
The Jade Emperor was astonished by the Dragon's good nature, and it was named as the fifth animal of the zodiac.
Cat instead of Rabbit and Bird instead of Rooster.
Although garnets are often associated with metamorphism, they can also occur in volcanic rocks on rare occasions.
Amethyst, a semiprecious stone, is often used in jewelry.
Peridot is one of the birthstones for the month of August.
Topaz is often mined in open-pit or alluvial settings.

editorNotes: No tile fits two groups here: Leo is a lion and Aries a ram, but the Chinese zodiac has no lion or ram, and the dragon is Chinese rather than a western sign. Topaz and garnet are gemstones and not signs.
